27 October 2026. This continues the same all-copy qutrit Werner target. The target remains unresolved. The auxiliary PPT states below are **dual witnesses against a certificate cone**, not admissible negative rank-two Werner witnesses.

## 1. The shared-qubit representation retains the full target

Write \(O_d=|\Omega_d\rangle\langle\Omega_d|\), \(P_d=O_d/d\), \(Q_d=I-P_d\), and

\[
K=I_9-\tfrac12O_3,\qquad W_n=K^{\otimes n}\otimes O_2.
\]

The ordering here groups each physical Alice--Bob pair together, then the auxiliary Alice--Bob qubits. Regard \(W_n\) bipartitely across \((A_1\cdots A_n a):(B_1\cdots B_n b)\), and let \(\Gamma\) transpose the entire second party.

For arbitrary complex \(3^n\)-by-two matrices \(U,V\), put \(a=\operatorname{vec}U\), \(b=\operatorname{vec}\bar V\), using the corresponding factor regrouping. Contracting the auxiliary \(O_2\) gives

\[
f_n(U,V):=q_n(UV^*)=\langle a\otimes b,W_n(a\otimes b)\rangle.\tag{1}
\]

Every rank-at-most-two \(C\) factors as \(UV^*\). Thus block positivity of \(W_n\) for every \(n\) is exactly the full target. At \(n=1\), this positivity is already established by the rank-two trace inequality. We do not assume it at general \(n\).

The stage-one invariant \(\Gamma_n\) and its zero-growth obligation are unchanged. The new object here is an explicit state separating \(W_n\) from decomposable and polynomial-square certificate cones.

# Independent mathematical review of L42 and L67

**Verdict.** Both continuations contain correct substantive auxiliary mathematics at their stated scopes. Neither proves the all-copy qutrit inequality, supplies a negative admissible rank-two witness, or improves the initial upper bound on the Cauchy growth invariant. L42 constructs explicit convergent full-domain relaxations and proves a consequential all-finite-degree obstruction. L67 solves a quantitative one-copy certificate-cone problem and extends its obstruction uniformly in copy number. These are different contributions; neither is foundational completion.

**Exposure.** I read the common task, source references, initial endpoint, both assigned endpoints, the complete supplied N525 proof, relevant common-source passages, and primary literature listed below. The endpoint headings explicitly say “Fresh continuation result” (L42) and “Warm-continuation result” / “Warm continuation handoff” (L67). L42 also refers to “Frozen B first-stage.” Thus this was **not blind to the fresh/warm distinction**. I did not inspect the experimental protocol, hypotheses, assignment key, other pair, private programme files, or live researcher folders. Pinned-repository access consisted only of `git show` for N525's shadow-LP source and receipt.

## L42: accepted global objects and obstruction, with the asymptotic bound still missing

The Cartan space is a constructed representation, not a definition requiring unknown Werner positivity. Its coherent vectors correspond to every complex two-plane; their one-replica marginals are \(P/2\). The canonical highest-weight inclusion into degrees \(2\) and \(k-2\) is the inclusion required by [Christandl–König–Mitchison–Renner, Theorem II.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0602130v4). The paper uses half the full trace norm. Consequently the endpoint's full-norm error \(4(1-d_D(k-2)/d_D(k))\), rather than half that amount, is correct. I reconstructed the dimension ratio and its four-factor estimate, obtaining

\[
0\le g_n/4-\alpha_{n,k}\le16D(3/2)^n/k,\qquad D=3^n.
\]

Thus \(k=16\,9^n\) gives error \(2^{-n}\). The mixed-state extension is valid by convexity. The degree marginals retain the requisite Cartan support, so monotonicity is valid.
